parsed.why: Strong national anti-discrimination and hate-crime law, courts enforce trans rights, and custody guidance protects preferences; but documented violence, discrimination, and divergent male-unit prison practice keep risk elevated.

Self-declaration, broad hate-crime law, high public support, and visible community; residual discrimination survey and healthcare gaps are mostly resident-facing, with no documented trans-specific visitor exposure.

Same-sex conduct criminalised with 2–5 years and deportation for foreigners, no reported arrests but military discretion, no protections, and no recourse; trans visitor read as same-sex risks severe statutory exposure.
Same-sex conduct decriminalised, but trans workers excluded from protections, a 2018 cleaver attack drew no jail, official hostility, and no recognition leave outed trans visitors with weak recourse.

State criminalises LGBTQIA+ practice and transition with 5–10 years, bans organisations, and documents coordinated arrests and imprisonments; outed trans visitors face severe, enforced state targeting.
